query: A TiVNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy has been reported in a single-phase BCC, dendritic state, with a yield strength of about 800 MPa and roughly 40% strain under lower-temperature testing, but at 1273 K it retains only 330 MPa yield strength and 423 MPa compressive strength at 30% strain. For its use as an intermediate layer that transfers heat between W and CuCrZr while preserving structural integrity, what single intervention could overcome this loss of strength at elevated temperature? State the proposed intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the reported baseline, define the applicable thermal and mechanical boundary conditions, identify supporting prior evidence, and propose a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a very small, uniform dispersion (≈1–2 vol %) of ultra-fine Y2O₃ nanoparticles into the single-phase BCC TiVNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy will more than offset its high-temperature softening; at 1273 K the 0.2 % offset yield strength will rise from ≈330 MPa (baseline) to ≥550 ± 50 MPa while retaining ≥25 % compressive plastic strain.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast TiVNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy, single-phase BCC, ~800 MPa yield strength at room temperature, ~330 MPa yield strength and 423 MPa flow stress at 30 % strain in compression at 1273 K; dendritic microstructure, no second phases.
generation.intervention: Mechanical alloying of Ti, V, Nb, Ta elemental powders with 1.5 vol % pre-synthesised 10–20 nm Y₂O₃, followed by spark-plasma sintering (≈1573 K, 50 MPa, 5 min) to obtain a fully dense ODS-TiVNbTa billet.
generation.conditions: Service and test temperature 1000–1273 K in vacuum or Ar; compressive strain rate 10⁻³ s⁻¹; thermal gradient imposed by contact with W (≈1500 K face) and CuCrZr (≈600 K face) but average layer temperature not exceeding 1273 K.
generation.structural_mediator: Stable, inter- and intragranular Y₂O₃ nanoparticles (~20 nm) pinning grain boundaries and acting as non-shearable obstacles to dislocations.
generation.mechanism: Dispersion strengthening via Orowan looping and dislocation climb suppression; oxide particles also act as vacancy sinks, retarding recovery and grain-boundary sliding, thereby maintaining dislocation density and fine grain size at 1273 K.
generation.predicted_outcome: 0.2 % YS ≈550 MPa, peak compressive stress at 30 % strain ≈650 MPa, plastic strain ≥25 %; creep rate at 1273 K and 200 MPa reduced by ≥1 order of magnitude compared with baseline TiVNbTa.
generation.baseline: 0.2 % YS 330 MPa, peak stress 423 MPa at 30 % strain, ≈40 % plastic strain at 1273 K for dendritic, precipitate-free TiVNbTa.
generation.boundary: Effectiveness expected up to ≈1400 K; above this temperature or for oxide volume fraction >3 % coarsening or embrittlement may negate the benefit. Must retain particle size <50 nm after 10 h at 1273 K for claim to hold.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate—ODS processing may introduce oxygen embrittlement or particle agglomeration; interfacial compatibility with W/CuCrZr and thermal fatigue resistance are not yet verified.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two billets: (a) baseline TiVNbTa (powder-metallurgy route without oxide) and (b) ODS-TiVNbTa with 1.5 vol % Y₂O₃, matched grain size by identical consolidation schedule except for oxide addition. Subject both to: i) compression at 1273 K, 10⁻³ s⁻¹ to 40 % strain, ii) constant-load compressive creep at 1273 K/200 MPa for 100 h, followed by TEM analysis of particle size and dislocation structure.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if the ODS material shows (i) ≤400 MPa yield strength at 1273 K OR <25 % improvement over baseline in yield or peak stress, OR (ii) plastic strain <15 % at 1273 K, OR (iii) creep rate reduction <3× relative to baseline.
